column2: On the authority of the Mother of the Believers, Umm ʿAbdillāh ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her), who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever introduces into this matter of ours what is not part of it, it is rejected.” Agreed upon (al-Bukhārī and Muslim).
In a narration of Muslim: “Whoever does a deed that is not in accordance with our matter, it is rejected.”

Aḥdatha (“introduces”): originates and invents. Fī amrinā (“into our matter”): into our religion. Radd (“rejected”): thrown back, not accepted; a verbal noun used in the sense of a passive participle.
Encouragement to follow [the Sunnah] and a warning against innovation.
The rejection of every newly introduced matter in the religion, with no difference between what a person introduces himself and what someone else introduces and he then acts upon.
Whatever conforms to the Sharīʿah or is covered by its general principles is not rejected.
The judgement of a judge does not change realities: it does not make the unlawful lawful or the lawful unlawful, even if it is carried out outwardly.
This hadith guides us to the fact that whoever worships through something not prescribed by Allah

and His Messenger, or introduces into the religion something not supported by any of its foundations in the Sunnah or its general principles, that is rejected and thrown back upon him, and he is sinful in doing it; and in any transaction, if something occurs in it that invalidates the contract because it contravenes the ruling of the Sharīʿah, it must be returned to its owner.
So let every Muslim beware of innovating in the religion and hold fast to the guidance of the master of the messengers ﷺ.
Be a follower of the Sunnah of the best of creation, / for it is the token of the servant's salvation.
He is the one whose favours have embraced creation, / and his kindness has reached them all in both abodes.
Since he came, hearts that were blind have seen through him / the paths of guidance, and ears have heeded the truth.
